extracted.intended_audience: K99/R00 applicants, mentors, and NIH reviewers (career development grant audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A K99/R00 candidate's career development and training plan describing training objectives, mentorship, didactic activities, competencies, specific aims, and measurable pilot outcomes to transition to an independent R01-funded investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 1: Extend knowledge in core substantive areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend knowledge in core substantive areas: hospice, dementia caregiving, and recruitment and retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with mentors and advisors and participate in didactic activities such as shadowing providers and attending grand rounds and team meetings to deepen understanding of clinical and real-world aspects of hospice care and dementia caregiving, how hospice organizations operate and deliver care, and recruitment and retention of vulnerable, hard-to-reach, and underrepresented groups (e.g., hospice patients, PwD, African American persons). Become a trainer in existing multi-site grants (e.g., Dr. Brody’s R33) to gain experience working with hospice organizations. Attend WCM and VNSNY grand rounds and Center for Research on End-of-Life Care meetings as scheduled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 2: Develop, implement, and disseminate behavioral interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop, implement, and disseminate behavioral interventions for older adults and home hospice clinicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in formal didactic experiences (coursework and training seminars) and work with mentors who are experts in intervention development. Learn best practices for developing rigorous interventions in clinical care settings, workforce training, goal attainment scaling, and community collaboration. Use acquired skills during K99 to develop a training and tool-based intervention for home hospice clinicians to support FCG of PwD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 3: Design and conduct clinical trials (RCT and pragmatic trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire expertise in designing and conducting randomized controlled trials and pragmatic trials to pilot and evaluate behavioral interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gain expertise through coursework, training institutes, protocol-writing workshops, and mentorship. Specific options listed include applying to the NIH Summer Institute on Randomized Behavioral Clinical Trials, completing Clinical Trials Design and Analysis and Clinical Trials: Trial Designs (WCM workshops), Protocol Writing Workshop (WCM), and the NIH Pragmatic and Group-Randomized Trials in Public Health and Medicine online course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 4: Professional development — grant writing and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop grant writing skills and build collaborative networks to prepare competitive R00 and R01 applications and multi-site trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in didactic workshops and national conferences, retake Responsible Conduct of Research training, complete WCM Planning and Writing Successful Grant Proposals workshop, apply to leadership programs (e.g., WCM Leadership in Academic Medicine), present at in-house work-in-progress sessions, and disseminate research at national conferences (GSA, AAHPM, ASA). Work with mentors to hone R00/R01 submission materials and cultivate collaborators for future multi-site studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship Team: interdisciplinary, committed mentorship with defined roles and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a strong, interdisciplinary team of mentors and advisors who provide guidance, hands-on training access, and support for the proposed research and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary mentor (Dr. Prigerson) oversees all aspects of the study, provides focused mentorship in EOL care, behavioral interventions, and RCTs, and supplies resources/support staff as needed. Mentors/co-mentors provide focused mentorship in dementia caregiving, recruitment/retention, workforce training, hospice/home care, goal attainment scaling, etc. Commitments include meeting frequency (e.g., weekly with primary mentor during K99; monthly with some co-mentors; quarterly/semi-annually during R00), letters documenting resources/support, and ongoing involvement during K99 with lighter touchpoints during R00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic experiences and training institutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include varied didactic experiences (shadowing, online coursework, in-person workshops, training institutes) to build competence across aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: NIH Training Institute on Dissemination and Implementation Research (4-month online + 2-day in-person) or Cornell Translational Research Summer Institute; Johns Hopkins Center for Innovative Care in Aging (Behavioral Interventions); AcademyHealth Science of Dissemination and Implementation conference; NIH Summer Institute on Randomized Behavioral Clinical Trials; WCM Clinical Trials Design and Analysis; WCM Protocol Writing Workshop (4-week); NIH Pragmatic and Group-Randomized Trials online course. Provide alternates if not accepted to a course.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 training activities: shadowing, grand rounds, center meetings, and hands-on training
rubrics_metrics.description: Hands-on experiential training in clinical settings and participation in institutional meetings to learn real-world operations and clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In year 1 of K99: shadow geriatrics physicians, hospice nurses, and social workers; attend WCM and VNSNY grand rounds and team meetings monthly; participate in Center on Research on End-of-Life Care weekly meetings; complete Hospice Champion Training (2 days); engage in training opportunities tied to mentors' projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency domains for career development (Table 1 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Twelve competency areas identified as necessary for the candidate: Workforce training; Community partner collaboration; Goal attainment scaling; RCTs and pragmatic trials; Responsible conduct of research; Professional development; End-of-life care; Hospice; Dementia caregiving; Recruitment and retention; Intervention development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each competency is linked to specific mentors/advisors with complementary expertise. The training plan should map mentors to competencies and show planned activities to build each competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aim 1 (K99 Y1): Identify common challenges, strategies, and gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1: To identify common challenges, strategies and gaps in care and support for community-dwelling PwD near the EOL; Sub Aim: identify commonalities and differences for African American and white FCG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods specified: semi-structured interviews with African American (n=20) and white (n=20) family caregivers and hospice clinicians (n=20) to identify challenges/strategies/gaps; a follow-up survey of hospice clinicians (n=80) to quantify frequency of occurrences at a large urban hospice provider. Use mixed-methods qualitative-to-quantitative approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aim 2 (K99 Y2): Adapt culturally inclusive training materials and create a goal assessment tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 2: Adapt dementia-focused training materials and create a goal assessment tool for home hospice clinicians to guide care and support for PwD and FCG; incorporate perspectives from diverse stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor existing dementia caregiving materials to home hospice challenges identified in Aim 1; design a tool that encompasses a culturally inclusive range of challenges, goals, and outcomes and that guides clinicians in tailoring care to individual FCG needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aim 3 (R00 Y1-Y2): Feasibility and acceptability benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 3: Examine feasibility and acceptability of the training and tool and revise based on feedback with explicit success thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses/benchmarks: >70% of home hospice clinicians will (1) complete the training, (2) report the training and tool are useful, (3) increase knowledge of dementia-related challenges and care strategies, and (4) increase confidence in providing dementia-related care. Use these thresholds to judge feasibility/acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aim 4 (R00 Y2-Y3): Pilot test preliminary efficacy with specified outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 4: Conduct a pilot test to determine preliminary efficacy of the training and tool compared to usual care on clinician knowledge, FCG burden, and PwD hospice disenrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesized outcomes: intervention clinicians will have greater knowledge and confidence, better ability to identify individual PwD/FCG challenges and suggest management strategies; FCG of intervention clinicians will report reduced burden; PwD of intervention clinicians will have lower rates of hospice disenrollment. Plan exploratory analyses to examine African American–white disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with NIA Stage Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the project to provide the NIA Stage Model sequence: Stage 0 (basic science), Stage 1A (development), and Stage 1B (preliminary testing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the study's phases (qualitative identification, adaptation/development, feasibility testing, pilot efficacy testing) to map explicitly onto Stage 0–1B so that the research yields foundational knowledge, intervention development, and preliminary efficacy data suitable for informing future R01 studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological approach: mixed methods with pilot testing and measurable sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mixed-methods (qualitative interviews, follow-up surveys, pilot trials) with pre-specified sample sizes and data collection plans appropriate to each aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: interview sample sizes (n=20 per subgroup), clinician survey (n=80), feasibility thresholds (>70% completion/usefulness/knowledge/confidence), and pilot trial outcomes for preliminary efficacy. Use these concrete methodological specifications to demonstrate feasibility and readiness for R00/R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance criterion: address growing population and disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate significance by addressing the growing number of PwD in home hospice and documented disparities (e.g., African American adults' higher dementia prevalence and worse hospice outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide epidemiologic context (projected dementia prevalence, proportions receiving hospice, disparities in pain management and disenrollment) and justify how the proposed intervention targets populations at elevated risk for suboptimal EOL outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for training/tool usefulness and clinician outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Define concrete, measurable outcomes to evaluate training and tool impact on clinician knowledge, confidence, perceived usefulness, and practice behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre/post measures and acceptability metrics (percent completing training, self-reported usefulness), objective knowledge/confidence scales, and downstream measures (FCG burden, hospice disenrollment) in pilot testing to assess intervention promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct and ethics training
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Responsible Conduct of Research training and other ethics training as part of professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retake WCM’s Responsible Conduct of Research course (semester-long, 11 contact hours) and include additional ethics training as outlined; ensure compliance and ethical preparedness for clinical research and trials.
